chunks: Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I was seated in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when Umm Khalid, who had been cut off by Yusuf ibn Umar, came in seeking permission to see him. Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'Would you like to hear her speech?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Grant her permission,' and he made me sit with him on the seat. Then she entered and spoke, and behold, she was an eloquent woman. She asked him about the two of them (the two caliphs). He said to her: 'Befriend them.' She said: 'Shall I say to my Lord when I meet Him that you ordered me to befriend them?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'But this one who is with you on the seat (Abu Baseer) orders me to keep away from them (Tabarra), while Kaseer al-Nawa orders me to befriend them. So which is better and more beloved to you?' He said: 'This one, by Allah, is more beloved to me than Kaseer al-Nawa and his companions. This one argues by saying: "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the unbelievers"; "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the unjust"; "And whoever did not judge by what Allah revealed, those are they that are the transgressors".'

key_terms.أُمُّ خَالِدٍ: Umm Khalid, a companion known for her eloquence and presence in the Imam's court.
key_terms.الطِّنْفِسَةِ: The seat or cushion, indicating the place of honor or teaching.
key_terms.تَوَلَّيْهِمَا: Befriend them / Show love to them (Wilayah).
key_terms.قَطَعَهَا: He cut her off (from his company or favor), a term indicating a specific social or spiritual distance.
key_terms.كَثِيرٌ النَّوَّاءُ: Kaseer al-Nawa, a companion known for his political alignment and narration style.
key_terms.يُوسُفُ بْنُ عُمَرَ: Yusuf ibn Umar, a prominent companion and narrator, often associated with the political establishment.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Imam's preference for Tabarra over Wilayah in the context of the two caliphs?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Imam’s nuanced approach to political pragmatism versus theological truth, as he permits Umm Khalid to claim allegiance to the caliphs for social ease while affirming that his own command for Tabarra (disavowal) is superior. The Imam grounds this preference in the Quranic triad of Kufr, Dhulm, and Fisq (5:44-45), arguing that the caliphs’ failure to judge by divine revelation constitutes a fundamental deviation that makes their authority less beloved than the Imam’s guidance. This narrative highlights the Shia scholarly distinction between outward conformity (Taqiyya) and inward conviction, emphasizing that the core issue is adherence to divine law rather than mere political submission.
